source_text: When is a quotient stack algebraic?

<STRUCT_0001>
In
Groupoids in Spaces, Section <REF_0001>
we have defined the quotient stack <MATH_0001> associated to a groupoid
<MATH_0002> in algebraic spaces. Note that <MATH_0003> is a stack
in groupoids whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces (see
Bootstrap, Lemma <REF_0002>
and
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma <REF_0003>)
and such that there exists an algebraic space <MATH_0004> and a <MATH_0005>-morphism
<MATH_0006> which is an ``fppf surjection''
in the sense that it induces a map on presheaves of isomorphism classes of
objects which becomes surjective after sheafification.
However, it is not the case that <MATH_0007> is an algebraic
stack in general. This is not a contradiction with
Theorem <REF_0004>
as the <MATH_0008>-morphism <MATH_0009> may not
be flat and locally of finite presentation.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
The easiest way to make examples of non-algebraic quotient stacks is
to look at quotients of the form <MATH_0010> where <MATH_0011> is a scheme and <MATH_0012>
is a group scheme over <MATH_0013> acting trivially on <MATH_0014>. Namely, we will see
below
(Lemma <REF_0005>)
that if <MATH_0015> is algebraic, then <MATH_0016> has to be flat and locally
of finite presentation. An explicit example can be found in
Examples, Section <REF_0006>.
